newsitem.title: USA: U.S. task force to review electric reliability.
newsitem.headline: U.S. task force to review electric reliability.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department set up a task force to evaluate the reliability of the U.S. power grid and set out an agenda for research to promote electricity reliability, a department official said Thursday.

"We're looking for the task force to essentially come up with an agenda for cooperative research on electric system reliability both under existing conditions and for the future that would reflect potential restructuring directions," said Paul Carrier, staff director of the task force.
The 21-member panel, to be led by former Congressman Philip Sharp, is set to hold its first meeting on Jan 16.
Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary set up the task force as she promised in a report this fall to the White House on two major blackouts in the Western United States this summer.

The outages in July and August raised concerns that the opening of power supply markets to competition and transfer of transmission responsibilities to independent operators might undermine reliable deliveries of electricity.
"Reliability is critical in a period when the electricity industry is being restructured to face the challenges of competition," O'Leary said in a statement.
Members of the task force, appointed for two years, include officials from utilities, environmental groups, state and federal agencies, and research experts.
While no consumer groups were represented, Carrier said the task force was designed to find ways to ensure that electricity supplies to homes, businesses and industry remain secure.
